response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT e.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), m AS (SELECT AVG(igm) AS mu FROM j), d AS (SELECT j.ID, j.SEX, j.igm, j.igm - m.mu AS dev FROM j CROSS JOIN m), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS avg_dev FROM d WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID AS ID, d.SEX AS SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation_from_overall_mean, d.dev - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg_deviation FROM d JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg_deviation DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each examination row is one entry, so a patient with several examinations can appear more than once. The overall mean is taken over all examination rows that match a patient and have a non-null aCL IgM.
Rows with a missing sex are excluded, because a missing sex matches no group. Rows with a missing aCL IgM have no deviation and are also excluded.
Ties in the excess value are broken arbitrarily.
